cards.title: Improve Event Match Quality to feed an accurate action rate
cards.summary: If Meta only sees a fraction of your conversions, it computes a lower estimated action rate than reality, eroding your auction position—so signal quality is a real if small lever.
cards.use_when: Setting up or auditing pixel/CAPI tracking, or when reported conversions clearly undercount actual sales.

cards.title: Avoid the Entity ID trap by engineering true concept diversity
cards.summary: Meta groups near-identical ads under one Entity ID, so 200 similar ads can register as ~20 unique entities and serve the same audience pool, wasting the rest of your volume.
cards.use_when: Building or auditing a creative library, or when adding many ad variations has produced no incremental reach or conversion lift.

cards.title: Use the 20% budget-increase rule correction: it's a lag effect, not a learning reset
cards.summary: The common advice not to raise budgets more than 20% has no Meta documentation behind it; apparent post-increase dips are delayed purchases from newly reached audiences.
cards.use_when: Planning budget scaling on a winning campaign, or interpreting a revenue dip immediately after a budget increase.

cards.title: Consolidate account structure to unify conversion data—but keep justified segmentation
cards.summary: Campaign and ad set structure exists to signal segmentation to the algorithm; over-splitting silos learning data, while consolidation pools it and tends to perform better across platforms.
cards.use_when: Auditing campaign/ad set/ad structure, or deciding whether two product lines or sub-brands should share a campaign.

cards.title: Treat unit economics as the scaling constraint, not platform tactics
cards.summary: Sustained scaling comes from higher AOV, LTV, and gross margin that fund higher sustainable bids; competitors with better economics can outbid you despite worse creative and structure.
cards.use_when: Setting acquisition budget ceilings, prioritizing between creative testing and offer/margin improvements, or diagnosing a ceiling on scale.

cards.title: Stop optimizing for relevance and quality directly—diversify instead
cards.summary: Ad quality and expected action rate are per-user diagnostics computed after the fact, so the actionable proxy is broader asset diversity that is relevant to more people.
cards.use_when: When a stakeholder asks you to 'improve ad relevance/quality score,' or when deciding how to invest creative effort.

cards.title: Prune deprecated targeting advice from your Meta playbook
cards.summary: Several widely repeated Meta tactics are outdated or undocumented—interests/lookalikes, cookie deprecation warnings, Lattice education, and the 20% budget rule—so audit inherited advice before acting on it.
cards.use_when: Reviewing an agency proposal, onboarding a new media buyer, or refreshing internal SOPs for Meta campaigns.

cards.title: Diagnose Stuck Meta Accounts by Audience Awareness Mix
cards.summary: High frequency and stalled cold reach usually mean your creative library is almost entirely product-aware, so the algorithm keeps serving it warm.
cards.use_when: When a Meta ad account is stuck at high frequency, can't spend into cold audiences, or won't scale despite raising budget, and you need to decide what to fix before touching targeting or bidding.

cards.title: The Five Stages of Customer Awareness for Ad Scripting
cards.summary: Define each awareness stage before writing so every ad meets the viewer where they actually are instead of where your product team wishes they were.
cards.use_when: Before writing any Meta ad script or static, when choosing what the hook, body and offer should assume about the viewer's knowledge.

cards.title: Allocate Creative Volume 80/10/10 Across Awareness Stages
cards.summary: Because the warm audience pool is small, production volume should be proportional to audience size: most assets at the top, few at the bottom.
cards.use_when: When planning a monthly creative production slate or reacting to a funnel that can't scale because the account is over-invested in retargeting assets.

cards.title: Structure Meta Adsets by Awareness Concept
cards.summary: Grouping adsets by the awareness stage each concept targets lets your existing concept structure work naturally with delivery.
cards.use_when: When setting up or reorganising Meta campaign/adset structure for a new creative batch.

cards.title: One Stage Per Ad, Moved Through Deliberately
cards.summary: You can start at one stage and pull viewers down the funnel within the ad, or hammer a single stage — but never wander between stages incoherently.
cards.use_when: When writing or auditing an ad and deciding whether it should stay in one awareness stage or walk the viewer through several.

cards.title: Use the Product Awareness Curve to Avoid Jarring Bridges to CTA
cards.summary: Viewer awareness that they're being sold to should rise slowly through the ad, not spike at the product reveal or call to action.
cards.use_when: When scripting a video ad and reviewing retention curves for where viewers drop off.

cards.title: Write Unaware Static Ads with Curiosity Image Plus Long-Form Story
cards.summary: Top-of-funnel statics can scale cold spend by pairing vague or seemingly unrelated imagery with primary text that pulls readers through a long narrative.
cards.use_when: When producing static creative for cold prospecting and you're tempted to reserve statics only for retargeting.

cards.title: Match Unaware Advertising to Cold Audiences, Not Problem Agitation
cards.summary: If the viewer doesn't know the problem exists, agitation is premature — start with a bold claim and reframe instead.
cards.use_when: When writing cold-traffic ads for a product or category where many prospects have no prior awareness of the underlying problem.

cards.title: Choose Solution-Aware for Mechanism-Led Ads
cards.summary: When viewers know the category but haven't picked a product, make your unique mechanism the centre of the creative.
cards.use_when: When advertising to audiences who have tried or researched competitors in your category, or when producing mid-funnel creative after top-of-funnel volume is running.

cards.title: Convert Product-Aware and Most-Aware Audiences with Proof and Offer
cards.summary: Bottom-of-funnel assets should stop convincing about the category and instead supply proof, risk reversal, offer clarity and a reason to act now.
cards.use_when: When building retargeting creative for site visitors, add-to-cart users or people who already know your product.

cards.title: Estimate an Ad's Awareness Stage by When the Product Appears
cards.summary: The later a video introduces the product, the further up-funnel the asset sits — a quick heuristic for auditing creative.
cards.use_when: When auditing a library of video or static creatives and needing a fast first-pass categorisation by intended audience.

cards.title: Diagnose inflated ROAS in Advantage+ scaling campaigns with audience breakdowns
cards.summary: Break a top-spending Advantage+ TOF ad down by audience (new vs existing vs engaged) to reveal when headline ROAS is really just retargeting existing customers.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a Meta Advantage+ top-of-funnel scaling campaign where a top-spending ad shows a very high platform ROAS and you need to decide whether to scale budget, brief more creative like it, or pull spend.

cards.title: Use 7-day click for optimization and treat incremental attribution as a breakout only
cards.summary: Optimize Meta campaigns on 7-day click (ignore view-throughs) and use Meta's incremental attribution only as a comparison column, because it is a modelled estimate, not a holdout result.
cards.use_when: Setting the attribution/optimization setting on any Meta cold or scaling campaign, or deciding whether to switch optimization toward incremental attribution because it looks 'more accurate'.

cards.title: Exclude existing customers from cold TOF campaigns, with a lapsed-customer carve-out
cards.summary: Block existing customers from cold scaling campaigns so spend cannot cannibalize retargeting, but segment long-lapsed buyers into their own campaign rather than hard-excluding them.
cards.use_when: Structuring a Meta cold/prospecting or Advantage+ top-of-funnel campaign and defining exclusion audiences, especially when attempting to scale and new-customer acquisition is flat while CAC rises.

cards.title: Measure scaling lift on top-line new-customer sales at the SKU level
cards.summary: Validate a TOF scaling campaign against top-line revenue (ideally new-customer sales on a specific SKU) rather than accepting in-platform ROAS as the success metric.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether a Meta TOF scaling campaign actually worked after a budget increase, or when total-revenue-based readouts are too noisy to reach significance in a reasonable test window.

cards.title: Why optimizing on 1-day view-through inflates rankings and misallocates spend
cards.summary: If the ad set optimizes on 7-day click plus 1-day view, spend concentrates on view-through-heavy ads, so the in-platform ranking of your best creatives is not trustworthy.
cards.use_when: Interpreting ad-level performance rankings in a Meta scaling campaign, or deciding which creative concepts to brief more of based on which ads are winning inside the account.

cards.title: Read purchase conversion separately from lead conversion when auditing a scaling campaign
cards.summary: Keep purchase-based campaign metrics distinct from lead-based ones, since the diagnosis of an inflated scaling campaign depends on conversions that end in sales, not leads.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a Meta cold acquisition campaign that runs on purchase events, or when a campaign's reported performance differs depending on whether leads or purchases are counted.

cards.title: Diagnostic path when CAC rises on every scaling attempt and new customers stay flat
cards.summary: When scale-ups raise CAC without raising new-customer acquisition, run a fixed three-check audit: retargeting overlap, over-attribution, and cold-spend cannibalization.
cards.use_when: A store repeatedly increases Meta budget and sees CAC climb while new-customer count stays flat, and you need a structured first-pass audit of the ad account.

cards.title: Match account complexity to business complexity
cards.summary: Right-size Meta account segmentation by auditing product categories, ranges, demographics and budget constraints before choosing campaign and adset layers.
cards.use_when: Setting up or restructuring a Meta ad account for a store with multiple product lines, seasonal ranges or creative volume goals.

cards.title: Judge creative at the adset level, not the ad level
cards.summary: Meta last-click attribution makes ad-level ROAS unreliable; move KPI evaluation and budget decisions up to the adset so data has integrity.
cards.use_when: Deciding which creatives to scale, pause or replicate when ad-level ROAS numbers conflict with spend.

cards.title: Define a concept as persona + angle + offer
cards.summary: Group adsets by concept — persona + angle + offer — so creative learnings roll up to a reliable, interpretable level.
cards.use_when: Organizing adsets for a high-volume creative testing program where you need to learn which messages work.

cards.title: Avoid launch-date adset segmentation
cards.summary: Batching new ads into adsets by the date they were made destroys targeting clarity because the adset is where Meta's audience learning lives.
cards.use_when: You are tempted to create a fresh adset each time you produce a new batch of creative.

cards.title: Keep conflicting personas out of one adset
cards.summary: Each Meta adset learns in isolation, so grouping unrelated audiences (e.g., men's and women's apparel) degrades delivery efficiency.
cards.use_when: Structuring adsets for a store targeting multiple distinct demographics or use cases.

cards.title: Use format segmentation only for new or low-spend accounts
cards.summary: Splitting adsets by format (image, video, DPA) stabilizes early soft-metric volatility but is counterproductive for mature accounts.
cards.use_when: Launching a brand-new Meta account or testing creative formats with limited conversion history.

cards.title: Segment by landing page only when it adds something Shopify can't tell you
cards.summary: Landing-page adset segmentation is possible but often redundant because Shopify already reports page-level conversion data.
cards.use_when: Considering whether to build adsets around homepage, product page, collection page or custom landing pages.

cards.title: Use adset-level category segmentation to reflect margin differences
cards.summary: When product categories have different gross margins, adset-level splits let you set different efficiency targets and spend distribution per category.
cards.use_when: Setting ROAS targets and spend distribution across product categories like dresses, tops, pants and accessories.

cards.title: Double down on winning concepts with 120 creatives instead of 50
cards.summary: After Pareto's principle concentrates spend in a few concepts, redirect creative production into the winners rather than spreading output evenly.
cards.use_when: Planning next month's creative production volume after an adset-level review shows one or two concepts dominating spend.

cards.title: Cap max spend share on any single winning adset
cards.summary: Instead of overleveraging into one winning concept, set a max spend percentage and keep rotating new concepts in to generate consistent learnings.
cards.use_when: A single concept adset is absorbing most budget and you want to limit business risk while continuing to scale.

cards.title: Make every structure defensible and commercially aligned
cards.summary: Any high-volume Meta structure must pass two tests: readable, integrity-preserving data, and alignment with the store's commercial objectives.
cards.use_when: Auditing an existing Meta account structure or designing one before scaling creative volume.

cards.title: Treat day-to-day bid and budget fiddling as low value
cards.summary: The source claims traditional media buying died around three years ago; the remaining high-leverage work is strategic account structure.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to spend your ad management time each week.

cards.title: Support high creative volume without breaking efficiency
cards.summary: A concept-segmented account with adset-level KPIing can absorb large monthly creative volume while still producing actionable learnings.
cards.use_when: Planning a high-volume creative testing pipeline and deciding how much creative the account can actually support.

cards.title: Audit as constraint diagnosis, not settings checklist
cards.summary: Structure an ad-account audit as a ranked diagnosis of the single business constraint, delivered as a prioritized 90-day roadmap.
cards.use_when: You are planning a quarterly audit of your paid media account or deciding whether an incoming audit document is worth acting on.

cards.title: Refuse to audit without business-level KPI access
cards.summary: An ad audit is only valid if you can see business KPIs (cost per new customer, gross profit), not just platform-reported ROAS.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether you can run a meaningful audit with the data you currently have access to, or selecting an agency that only reports platform metrics.

cards.title: Build a 2–2.5 year CAC and GP-per-customer cohort model
cards.summary: Graph monthly CAC, gross profit on first purchase, and new-customer volume over 2–2.5 years to see whether efficiency is trending right or wrong.
cards.use_when: You need a top-level read on whether your paid acquisition economics are improving or deteriorating before drilling into platforms.

cards.title: GP-to-CAC ratio bands for scale, hold, or pull back
cards.summary: Use first-purchase gross profit divided by CAC to judge whether current economics justify scaling spend.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to increase ad budgets, hold flat, or cut spend based on first-order profitability.

cards.title: Normalized P&L for volume verification
cards.summary: Build a 2–2.5 year normalized P&L to check whether contribution margin improves or degrades as you ramp ad spend.
cards.use_when: You are verifying whether scaling ad spend produced profitable volume or just bought top-line revenue.

cards.title: First-time-customer P&L to expose weak acquisition
cards.summary: Filter out returning-customer revenue to see true new-customer acquisition performance and compute acquisition MER.
cards.use_when: Your blended P&L looks healthy but you suspect paid acquisition is actually underperforming.

cards.title: Reconcile platform ROAS with acquisition MER
cards.summary: Detect over-attribution by comparing platform account-wide ROAS against the acquisition MER from your first-time P&L.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to trust Meta, Google, TikTok, or Pinterest reported ROAS for budget decisions.

cards.title: Google: check brand/non-brand split and non-brand correlation
cards.summary: Keep brand and non-brand campaigns cleanly separated and test non-brand ROAS against acquisition MER.
cards.use_when: You are evaluating whether Google Search/Shopping is genuinely acquiring new customers or harvesting existing demand.

cards.title: Isolate a test to resolve attribution ambiguity
cards.summary: When correlation between platform ROAS and business MER stays unresolved, run a controlled incrementality test instead of guessing.
cards.use_when: You cannot tell whether a platform (Meta, Google, TikTok) is genuinely driving incremental new-customer revenue.

cards.title: Evaluate retention to set CAC targets
cards.summary: Benchmark gross-profit retention curves by day 90, 180, and 365 to decide how much first-purchase CAC you can tolerate.
cards.use_when: You are setting acquisition budget targets and need to know whether high first-order CAC is justified by repeat purchasing.

cards.title: One cold campaign until business complexity forces a split
cards.summary: Start account structure from a single cold campaign and require a defendable purpose for every additional campaign.
cards.use_when: You are restructuring a Meta or Google ad account or reviewing whether campaign count is inflated.

cards.title: Check frequency across new, engaged, and existing audiences
cards.summary: Use 30-day frequency on new/engaged/existing segments to find overspend and weak top-of-funnel content.
cards.use_when: You are diagnosing audience-segment budget distribution or diagnosing creative fatigue in your Meta account.

cards.title: Standardize on 7-day click plus 1-day engaged view
cards.summary: Adopt a single tight attribution setting across the account and keep it consistent.
cards.use_when: You are configuring Meta attribution settings or auditing whether settings are inconsistent across campaigns.

cards.title: Audit campaign naming against actual settings and creative
cards.summary: Confirm that campaign/adset naming matches the targeting, objective, and creative actually running underneath.
cards.use_when: You are doing a housekeeping pass or suspect high-ROAS 'cold' campaigns are mislabeled warm or existing-customer campaigns.

cards.title: Common Meta settings errors worth fixing
cards.summary: A short list of concrete Meta account errors: undefined segments, App Rewards placements, legacy lookalike/interest targeting on purchase objectives, missing existing-customer exclusions.
cards.use_when: You are doing a settings-and-targeting error sweep on a Meta account during a structure audit.

cards.title: Google-specific audit checks: search terms, feed, currency
cards.summary: Audit Google by checking brand leakage in cold campaigns, Merchant Center feed completeness, and multi-currency feed setup.
cards.use_when: You are auditing Google Ads and Google Merchant Center ahead of a seasonal peak or a restructure.

cards.title: Creative volume rule: one new ad per $1,000 of monthly spend
cards.summary: Size your creative production requirement by anchoring new ads per month to monthly ad spend.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether creative volume is the bottleneck or setting a production target for your creative team or agency.

cards.title: Separate volume, diversity, and quality as the creative bottleneck
cards.summary: Creative bottlenecks are one of exactly three: insufficient volume, insufficient concept diversity, or insufficient quality.
cards.use_when: You are diagnosing why creative performance has plateaued and need to pick the right fix.

cards.title: Diversify concepts, not just formats
cards.summary: Measure creative diversity by angle/offer/persona concept coverage rather than by mix of UGC, statics, and other formats.
cards.use_when: You are planning creative strategy for a scaling account or diagnosing why a single winning ad fatigues.

cards.title: Don't over-allocate to dynamic product ads
cards.summary: Keep DPAs as a small share of spend because they are bottom-of-funnel and rarely incremental.
cards.use_when: You are rebalancing spend inside a Meta account where DPAs are consuming the majority of budget.

cards.title: Analyze winners to replicate the source of success
cards.summary: When an ad wins, diagnose which variable caused the win and consciously replicate that variable.
cards.use_when: You have recently found a winning creative and are deciding whether to iterate on it or chase entirely new ideas.

cards.title: Run creative production as a system with a feedback loop
cards.summary: Replace ad-hoc creative production with a continuous system that ingests performance feedback.
cards.use_when: You are setting up or reviewing your creative roadmap and production cadence against a scale target.

cards.title: Drill down from business metrics to the ad that's the bottleneck
cards.summary: Trace a constraint top-down from business revenue to platform, campaign, adset, and ad to locate the actual driver.
cards.use_when: You have identified a top-level problem (e.g., rising CAC) and need to find where in the account it lives.

cards.title: Fix data integrity before creative or account structure
cards.summary: If platform metrics do not correlate with business KPIs, treat that as the top-priority bottleneck before anything else.
cards.use_when: You are sequencing a paid-media turnaround and deciding what to fix first.

cards.title: Ad account audit order: data → structure → creative
cards.summary: A prioritization sequence for auditing underperforming paid ad accounts: fix data integrity first, then account structure, then creative.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing a declining or flat paid acquisition program (Meta/Google) and deciding which fix to tackle first this quarter.

cards.title: Write ads as salesmanship in print
cards.summary: Claude Hopkins' core test: every ad, headline, and creative decision should be judged by whether it would help a live salesperson close the sale to one prospect standing in front of him.
cards.use_when: Writing or reviewing any acquisition creative — Meta/TikTok ad, product page hero, landing page, or email subject line — and you need a single test to cut indecision.

cards.title: Sell service, not your brand
cards.summary: Hopkins argues the two greatest faults in advertising are boasts and selfishness; replace 'buy my brand' appeals with a clearly unselfish offer of service to the customer.
cards.use_when: Drafting ad copy or landing page hero sections where the instinct is to lead with the brand name, product features, or company achievements.

cards.title: Advertise to one person, not the masses
cards.summary: Treat every inquirer as an individual prospect who walked into a store, with a specific need — not as a mass to be sent the same generic catalog or ad.
cards.use_when: Setting up email capture, retargeting sequences, PDP recommendations, or paid traffic flows where all visitors currently get the same generic response.

cards.title: Tell the pains you take (the Schlitz story)
cards.summary: Reveal the ordinary manufacturing and quality steps you take, even if competitors do the same, because nobody has told the story in print and it creates perceived distinction.
cards.use_when: Writing a product page, brand story section, or ad angle for a commodity-like product where you believe 'everyone does this, so it's not a differentiator.'

cards.title: Sell painkillers, not prevention
cards.summary: Prevention and disaster-avoidance are weak appeals; Hopkins found people will do anything to cure a trouble but little to prevent it, so advertise rewards, beauty, happiness, and desirable outcomes.
cards.use_when: Choosing the angle for health, wellness, supplement, dental, financial, or maintenance-focused products where the default pitch is risk prevention.

cards.title: Sample the right way: require an effort
cards.summary: Free samples and demos work only when the user requests them or earns them; promiscuous sampling destroys perceived value, so gate samples behind an action.
cards.use_when: Designing lead magnets, free-trial offers, sample distribution, or PR-box mailers — deciding whether to send product free or require an opt-in.

cards.title: Give your brand a human personality
cards.summary: People love people more than corporations; giving your product or brand a named, personal spokesperson makes the creation famous along with the person.
cards.use_when: Building brand identity, creator-led content, founder-led marketing, or repositioning a faceless ecommerce brand in categories where competitors are all 'soulless corporations.'

cards.title: Test, never assume your own taste predicts demand
cards.summary: Hopkins warns that judging products by personal preference has cost the advertising industry fortunes — the successes he doubted sold like crazy, so submit everything to the court of public opinion through testing.
cards.use_when: Deciding what products, creatives, or angles to launch or kill when you have a personal gut reaction for or against them.

cards.title: Stay close to the buyer and the money
cards.summary: Hopkins advises studying actual sellers (including canvassers and door-to-door salesmen) to learn what appeals work, and positioning your work near revenue-generating activity so you can capture a share of the value created.
cards.use_when: Doing customer research for ad angles, or negotiating roles, contracts, or agency compensation tied to advertising and sales performance.

cards.title: Stick with the ad that works (moving parade)
cards.summary: You notice your own ads far more than customers do; Hopkins warns against changing successful campaigns out of boredom and says the best way to win new customers is usually the way that won millions.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to refresh or replace a profitable creative, offer, or PDP hero because it 'feels stale' internally.

cards.title: Judge advertising by salesmanship and the customer's mind
cards.summary: Hopkins treats advertising as multiplied salesmanship whose success or failure is determined by whether the psychological appeal matches human nature — not by cleverness or personal taste.
cards.use_when: Choosing an appeal/angle before writing a campaign, or diagnosing why a campaign isn't converting despite decent execution.

cards.title: Prove the product, don't just talk about it
cards.summary: A dramatic demonstration converts far better than any argument; Hopkins sold roughly one in ten women by talk but nearly all by demonstration, and carried that principle into every campaign.
cards.use_when: Designing acquisition creative, PDP media, or landing page proof sections that currently rely on claims instead of showing the product working.

cards.title: Capitalizing on insights: put your money where your copy is
cards.summary: Hopkins bought shares in the brand whose sales his advertising would lift, capturing the value he helped create — a model for tying compensation or investment to measurable performance you drive.
cards.use_when: Structuring performance-based deals, agency compensation, affiliate arrangements, or deciding how to bet on a product angle you believe will outperform.

cards.title: Do the work in volume with focus
cards.summary: Hopkins attributes his success to exceptional hours and volume of practice, not exceptional ability: working two or three times as much produces two or three times the mistakes and successes, and you learn from both.
cards.use_when: Building a sustainable creative testing cadence or deciding how much output an in-house or agency ecommerce marketing function should produce.

cards.title: Reframe advertising questions around the buyer's desires
cards.summary: Almost every ad question can be answered by asking what a good salesman would say if the individual prospect stood before him — starting with the prospect's expressed desires, not your product facts.
cards.use_when: Resolving copy, offer, or page-layout debates inside a team where opinions conflict and no test data yet exists.

cards.title: Don't let success in one area convince you you can run any
cards.summary: Hopkins observes men make money in one business and lose it in others because success breeds the belief that they are super-businessmen — past success is not transferable competence.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to expand your store into an unrelated product category, new market, or a different business, especially when an existing product line is performing well.

cards.title: Earn the role by demonstrating the work, not just applying
cards.summary: When Hopkins wanted a senior advertising job at a company with one of the largest budgets, he had dozens of people write testimonials, ran a daily newspaper column sharing his learning, and applied alongside the evidence — and won the role.
cards.use_when: Pitching a major retailer partnership, applying for an in-house leadership role, or winning a large client when you have no direct relationship and the competition is strong.
